item.title: Rockstar Games has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6, showcasing the game's unbelievable graphics, and fans can't believe it's real.
item.description:
Rockstar has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6, and like yesterday's footage, fans can't quite believe it's real.
This morning, the Instagram account "Only in Dade" (which posts real videos from around Miami, Florida) shared a video of several flashy cars driving around. However, this footage isn't real life; it's actually GTA 6 footage.
The page posted footage of these cars sitting on GTA 6's version of Ocean Drive yesterday while a group of NPCs observed them. Yesterday's footage was actually an in-game recreation of a real video that was posted in October, showing Rockstar's real-life marketing efforts in Miami. Presumably, the new video posted today is also a recreation of a real video from when the real versions of these cars were zooming around the city.
Although the footage doesn't show much, it is an extremely impressive showcase of GTA 6's graphical fidelity. When the first clip dropped yesterday, many thought it was AI or some kind of render. However, it has since been confirmed as authentic gameplay and was reposted by Rockstar itself on Instagram. Fans have reacted to both clips in awe of the visuals, noting that the game has really outdone itself.
"Absolutely insane this is in-game," said one fan in response to the new footage. "This game isn't real, bro; there HAS to be a trap somewhere. There is no f**king way," said another fan in disbelief.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
Some have even joked that if this is really how the final game looks, they're more than happy to play it at 30fps. It's clear that Rockstar traded higher performance in favor of visual fidelity, and while that may not be what some fans want, it is inevitably going to result in one of the most graphically advanced games we have ever seen.
Today officially marks exactly one week until GTA 6's release. The game is available to preload right now and it is tracking to have one of the biggest launches in entertainment history. Xbox and PlayStation both confirmed that the game is the most preordered title in the history of their respective stores, and analysts have estimated that the game has already surpassed $1 billion in sales ahead of launch.
Speaking of launch, some game developers are giving their staff the week off to play the game. Palworld developer Pocketpair is one such studio happy to provide extra holiday for the occasion. IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer.

item.title: Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope.
item.description:
Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope.
George Lucas' original Star Wars film debuted back in 1977, kicking off what would become one of the world's most popular and lucrative film and TV franchises. Half a century on, Disney+ will debut "The Hero Awakens," a brand-new documentary featuring rare archival footage from A New Hope's production, helmed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker R.J. Cutler.
The Hero Awakens will drop via Disney+ on Star Wars' annual May 4th celebration, following the theatrical re-release of Star Wars on February 19. This will be the rarely-seen original 1977 version of the movie — back when Jabba the Hutt was not a CGI slug and Greedo actually shot first.
In terms of what's actually new for the Star Wars franchise next year, Ahsoka Season 2 will drop via Disney+ on January 20, while Star Wars: Starfighter will land in theaters on May 28.
Both are anticipated, though will arrive at a time of great uncertainty for the Star Wars franchise in general, following the decidedly mixed response to Disney's sequel trilogy, several short-lived Disney+ TV projects, and a lengthy slate of movie projects cancelled or stuck in development hell. Not even a big screen outing for The Mandalorian and Grogu this year could turn things around, as the movie set a rather disappointing record for the franchise's lowest live-action theatrical gross.
Looking further ahead, a press release for Star Wars' 50th anniversary states that 2027 will bring a year of "new project announcements, anniversary merchandise, dedicated fan events, archival releases, and reimagined Disney Parks and Cruiseline offerings." Exactly what these project announcements are remains to be seen, though it seems likely we'll get a sense of the franchise's future before next year is out.
How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend
With Ahsoka and Starfighter the only remaining live-action Star Wars TV and movie projects publicly announced, the time has certainly come for Lucasfilm's newly-installed co-president Dave Filoni to map out what's next. Reports suggest that of everything Lucasfilm has previously announced, the new movie/trilogy written by Dark Phoenix's Simon Kinberg is the one currently moving forward.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."
item.description:
Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."
Sharma's essay, posted today on X/Twitter ahead of Xbox's quarter century anniversary this weekend, seems to take pains not to explicitly reference A.I. by name. But in a section looking ahead to the future of the Xbox brand and video games in general, the huge role that Sharma apparently believes A.I. will play is made pretty clear.
"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," Sharma wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable trade-off of ambition. We must change this.
The 100 Best Xbox Games of All Time
"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break," Sharma continued. "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."
It's hard to imagine that this version of the future could be possible without the heavy use of A.I. tools in game development — a topic that is still highly controversial among video game fans, even as it becomes all the more ubiquitous behind the scenes.
For industry watchers, though, and also for Xbox employees, Sharma's message also points to something else: a vision of game creation that's far leaner than now in terms of financial cost and human investment. After a another year of brutal layoffs across the video games industry and within Xbox in particular, this concept will likely do little to reassure anyone currently at the games development coalface.
Which Xbox console generation is your favorite so far?

item.title: Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.
item.description:
Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.
“All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches,” the company said in a tweet. The company also shared a letter it presumably sent out internally to workers at the studio.
“To all employees,” the letter started. “On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
“At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday.
The holiday period starts on GTA 6 launch date, November 19, and ends on November 23. “During this period, employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to take a business trip to Vice City,” the letter said.
“We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.”
All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.Please see the attached notice for details. https://t.co/qJjJ7IvhhY
Pocketpair boss Takuro Mizobe tweeted to confirm he'll be making the most of the special holiday, saying: "Of course, I’ll be taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too!"
Pocketpair isn’t the only company talking about GTA 6’s launch. The developer behind Wardogs encouraged its players to “go play GTA 6” and come back to the game after its next big update. Hardware company Logitech also announced that it will be giving employees time off for GTA 6. According to a new report, GTA 6 has caused a 17% spike in people requesting time off work, so it’s probably for the best.
Not long now! GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer, and the release of new GTA 6 footage that looks so real fans actually thought it was real-life.

item.title: The pitch for Sankan, from solo developer Dany Rexton of YTKA Games, intrigued me. "You and up to two friends work the night shift at a mountain gas station in Japan, 1999," he told me via email. "The voice in your head names a customer you have to kill. Do it, and you clean up the blood and bury the body before dawn. Refuse the voice, and it starts hunting you." And then I took a look at the moody, somewhat creepy trailer, complete with the built-in nostalgia of its PS1-era graphics, and I wanted to know more.
item.description:
The pitch for Sankan, from solo developer Dany Rexton of YTKA Games, intrigued me. "You and up to two friends work the night shift at a mountain gas station in Japan, 1999," he told me via email. "The voice in your head names a customer you have to kill. Do it, and you clean up the blood and bury the body before dawn. Refuse the voice, and it starts hunting you." And then I took a look at the moody, somewhat creepy trailer, complete with the built-in nostalgia of its PS1-era graphics, and I wanted to know more.
Sankan is planned for release on PC in early 2027. And it's not just a single-player game. Up to three people can play together cooperatively. Everyone speaks in subtitles, as there is no dialogue. Rexton says there are "several" endings. Check out that trailer above, and take a look at the first screenshots in the gallery below.
Sankan - First Screenshots
"The people you met come back in later shifts. So does what you did," Rexton told me. Again, it's intriguing. If you'd like to follow along with development as the early 2027 release target nears, you can wishlist Sankan on Steam.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is now complaining after Claude AI maker Anthropic finally introduced copyright limitations.
item.description:
A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is now complaining after Claude AI maker Anthropic finally introduced copyright limitations.
Claude models are now "starting to refuse" to work on projects that include official Pokémon assets, according to Pocket Monster fan Big Kid Nation. In a post on X/Twitter last night, Big Kid Nation went on to lament the fact that no money had ever been made on the project despite significant investment, unlike other similar projects that are being funded through Patreon.
"Anthropic has cracked down and Claude models are starting to refuse work on Pokémon fan projects," Big Kid Nation wrote, attaching a screenshot in which Claude stated it could no longer generate code designed to work with images it detected as featuring official Pokémon designs.
The Best Pokémon Spin-off Games
"All that money spent, never took a cent (unlike many others with itch.io, Patreon etc.)," Big Kid Nation continued. "Nintendo. Just make the epic Pokémon game you know we all want. I'll live on the street and work for free if it helps."
Big Kid Nation is currently building "Pokémon Arena 2D," a game that has somehow escaped the beady eyes of The Pokémon Company's lawyers up to this point, but seems unlikely to do so for much longer. "Real-time arena battles in pixel art," reads a description listed on BigKidNation.com. "Two years in the making, and free to play."
In another X/Twitter post made earlier this month, Big Kid Nation claimed they were racking up as much as "$2,000 expenses a month and 10-14 hour days both learning and building for most of this year and last." And while the game was coded using AI tools, Big Kid Nation was keen to push back on those branding it simply as "AI slop."
Big Kid Nation said that they set their PC running overnight simulating battles within Pokémon Arena 2D to try and detect balance issues, and then spent 14 hours a day sitting at the computer itself.
"Vibe coding games is so fun," Big Kid Nation wrote in another post, made last month. "There are some negatives with unethical vibe coders. But you're creative and love game development it's just a dream. What took me a year to make people can make in a week. And some can't make anything original. But those with ideas it's just one thing after another."
As an example of another "original vibe coded project", Big Kid Nation pointed to the separately-developed Poké Derby, which appears to be a Pokémon-themed version of the hugely popular Japanese racehorse game Umamusume. "This is what I'm talking about," Big Kid Nation wrote. "Instead of seeing ideas and just taking them with no creativity, these guys just build their own unique world from scratch."
Numerous comments on this post pointed out the fact this was in fact a Pokémon-themed version of Umamusume, seemingly to no avail.
The next official Pokémon games to release remain Pokémon Winds and Waves, which will arrive exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2 next year. Maybe it's best to just wait for those?

item.title: Popeyes has unveiled its new "Spice City" chicken sandwich, which is the restaurant's attempt to ride the hype wave for GTA 6.
item.description:
Popeyes has unveiled its new "Spice City" chicken sandwich, which is the restaurant's attempt to ride the hype wave for GTA 6.
Popeyes has confirmed that the Spice City chicken sandwich will be available in participating stores on November 19, the same day as Rockstar's highly anticipated release. The fast food chain said this new menu item is meant to "pay homage" to a sandwich in-game (it's unclear what in-game sandwich they are referring to, but there are drive-thrus and restaurants in GTA 6).
The sandwich includes two crispy chicken breast fillets stacked between a buttery, toasted brioche bun, topped with pickles and your choice of spicy or regular mayo. It'll set you back $6 (prices vary by location) and will be available from November 19 through November 22.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
A big part of this news is that the sandwich will be available for delivery through the Popeyes app and other food delivery services, so you don't have to leave your house or worry about cooking when GTA 6 releases.
"It’s been reported that a lot of fans will be calling in sick and are clearing their calendars to disappear into the sunniest, most chaotic open world in gaming," reads a Popeyes press release. "Popeyes has the perfect getaway meal and we wanted to let you know now so you can plan ahead."
It's just one of many ways the entire world seems to be getting on board with GTA 6. In addition to a wide-ranging marketing campaign from Rockstar itself, other companies have been attaching themselves to the hype train in unofficial ways. Logitech announced that it will be giving employees the day off for video game releases going forward and will be hosting a special live-streamed event on November 19 to celebrate this perk.
Spectrum and Xfinity are also offering free internet upgrades to allow customers the chance to download GTA 6 faster. It's clear that this has become a major, global event, and companies seem to be helping advertise GTA 6 at no cost to Rockstar. Xbox and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game in both of their respective histories, highlighting the extreme hype for the title. Those who have pre-ordered GTA 6 can pre-load the game now, and they will likely want to because the game is massive.
Rockstar also confirmed that GTA 6 will run at 30fps, but will have a few enhancements for PS5 Pro users. The news came as a bit of a disappointment for some fans who were hoping for a higher frame rate, but there is hope that maybe a potential PC or PS6 port could unlock better performance later down the line.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993. An interim boss has been appointed by Nvidia’s board of directors.
item.description:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993. An interim boss has been appointed by Nvidia’s board of directors.
Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, is appointed Interim CEO, Nvidia said. Harvey C. Jones was appointed its first-ever Chair of the Board.
In a statement, Nvidia's Board of Directors confirmed that Huang had resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. The Board said the search was on for a permanent CEO and "will consider internal and external candidates."
Nvidia GeForce RTX 30-Series Reveal
Who is Colette Kress?
Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has been its Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since then. She leads the gargantuan company's finance organization. Before Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
“Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the Nvidia Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”
“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress commented. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”
Why has Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO?
Nvidia's Board of Directors and the FBI launched an investigation into the 63-year-old Huang after he admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy. The New York Times then reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company. Stocks in the company fell on the news.
Nvidia provides advanced computer chips for everything from video games to cloud servers, but in recent years it has focused on the AI industry. Off the back of the enormous demand for memory to power data centers, Nvidia has become the world’s second-most valuable company, worth more than $4 trillion.
The prospect of Huang losing his job at Nvidia sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Tim Sweeney, boss of Fortnite developer Epic Games, was vocal in his support for Huang. He tweeted: “This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America. The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”
Reacting to the news of Huang's exit today, Sweeney tweeted: "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction."
What happens next?
Nvidia released the standard exit statement on Huang's departure, saying his controbutions to the company were "profound."
"Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world," the statement continued. "The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."
Nvidia will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, and all eyes will be on the company for news of a plan for the future.
Meanwhile, Huang is now potentially on the market as a competitor to the company he built. Yesterday, SpaceX, Telsa, and X owner Elon Musk tweeted to say it would be "an honour" to work with Huang.
Whatever Huang decides to do next, his days of showing off Nvidia graphics cards live on-stage during flashy presentations are over.
Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Tech billionaire Elon Musk has said it “would be an honor” to hire Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, who is currently under investigation from his own board of directors and the FBI after admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy.
item.description:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk has said it “would be an honor” to hire Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, who is currently under investigation from his own board of directors and the FBI after admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy.
The board of Nvidia is reportedly considering whether to oust its CEO. Stocks in the company have fallen on the news, and the New York Times has reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company.
The prospect of the 63-year-old Huang losing his job at Nvidia, which he co-founded in 1993, has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Nvidia provides advanced computer chips for everything from video games to cloud servers, but in recent years it has focused on the AI industry. Off the back of the enormous demand for memory to power data centers, Nvidia has become the world’s second-most valuable company, worth more than $4 trillion.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 30-Series Reveal
Nvidia’s board may decide to keep Jensen Huang on. Certainly tech executives have been calling for such a decision. Tim Sweeney, boss of Fortnite developer Epic Games, has been vocal in his support for Huang. He tweeted: “This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America.
“The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”
It’s worth noting that Sweeney is all-in on AI, and recently triggered a “huge pivot” of his company to retool it for “maximum AI acceleration.”
The board may, however, dismiss Huang and appoint a successor on an interim basis. Or, Huang resigns, putting himself on the market as a potential competitor to the company he built. In that scenario, Elon Musk may make a move. The Tesla owner took to his own social media platform, X, to say it would be "an honour" to work with Huang at SpaceX.
While Huang clearly has the backing of his fellow leaders in tech, he faces calls to resign from several U.S. lawmakers. There is also a reported move to tighten Nvidia China exports. Beijing has warned the U.S. not to use the spying allegations as a pretext to once again restrict tech sales to China.
Photographer: Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

item.title: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann has given a seemingly promising update on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and offered a fresh tease of what to expect.
item.description:
Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann has given a seemingly promising update on the studio's long-awaited Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and offered a fresh tease of what to expect.
PlayStation's upcoming, under-wraps space blockbuster remains largely a mystery, despite being revealed almost two years ago at The Game Awards in December 2024. We know only fragments of its story, and still have no idea when it will launch.
Speaking at the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, Druckmann said Intergalactic was now moving into its "last stages of production" and that the game was playable, with work now focusing on "refining and polishing." More intriguingly still, Druckmann described Intergalactic as an amalgamation of three other famous Naughty Dog franchises, with elements included from each.
Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Screenshots
"We used to have another game franchise called Jak and Daxter," Druckmann began. "And with this one, we really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi fantasy, the action-adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the more kind of serious drama we got for The Last of Us, and it really is a combination of those three franchises.
"We wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," he added. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing and go even deeper with gameplay systems?"
From the little that's been revealed of Intergalactic so far, we know that it will be an alternate universe sci-fi tale starring a bounty hunter stranded on a distant planet in the far future. This bounty hunter is Jordan A. Mun, played by Tati Gabrielle, with her bounty targets played by a roster of famous faces including Tony Dalton, Kumail Nanjiani and Ashley Scott. Naughty Dog regular Troy Baker is also set to appear.
Back in 2025, Intergalactic was reported to still be a couple of years from release, though PlayStation and Naughty Dog have refrained from narrowing its release window officially. That said, Druckmann recently indicated that the game would get a full unveiling at some point in the next 12 months.
If it feels like a while since you've played something new from Naughty Dog, arguably PlayStation's most high-profile studio, you're not wrong. Naughty Dog's last all-new release was The Last of Us Part 2, which released back in 2020. The intervening years have seen the studio launch various remasters, and scrap a multiplayer The Last of Us spinoff after years of work.
Intergalactic is just one of several projects in development at Naughty Dog, however, and fans now widely believe a new installment of Uncharted is also in the works.

item.title: GTA 6 was almost too much for South Korean ratings board GCRB, who struggled to agree whether the game should be approved or not. The board cited “out of context genital nudity” as the sticking point.
item.description:
GTA 6 was almost too much for South Korean ratings board GCRB, who struggled to agree whether the game should be approved or not. The board cited “out of context genital nudity” as the sticking point.
Rockstar sent an application for a South Korean rating on September 1. The initial vote, held on September 10, ended in a tie, with three votes for classification refusal and three for an Adults Only rating.
InvenGlobal acquired the meeting minutes from the voting sessions, where some board members argued for classification refusal over in-game nudity. When voting resulted in a tie, they chose to postpone the decision while awaiting a playable build of the game.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
A GTA 6 build was delivered to the committee on September 28 and an initial revisit of the board was postponed twice for a more "sufficient gameplay examination.” That’s one way to get to play it early.
After being initially pushed from October 2 to October 8, it was pushed once more and the committee met again on October 18. The second review passed a vote for an Adults Only rating with eight voting in favor of the rating and one voting against classification.
The content descriptors were assigned as “Sensuality, Violence, Crime, Drugs, and Language.” That first one, “Sensuality,” was the issue.
According to the report, the committee took particular issue with male nudity without any sexual context. The South Korean ratings board revised its regulation rules in September 2025, but previously even a suggestion of nudity could land a game with an Adults Only rating.
After the revision, this wording changed to "cases where suggestive bodily exposure is directly and specifically depicted." GTA 6 was the first game to run into the new, apparently more relaxed, rules. No such rules exist for crime or drug depictions.
A rating refusal would have blocked the release of GTA 6 in South Korea entirely. According to the report, the ratings board felt pressure with potentially being the sole country to refuse classification to the biggest game of the year.
Last month, GTA 6 received an age rating of PEGI 18, which included mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more. The rating, since deleted, described GTA 6's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time."
The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on "strong sexual themes," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." None of this should come as much of a surprise, given the GTA 6 launch trailer teases steamy shower scenes between Jason and Lucia.
Not long now: GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. item.title: Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
item.description:
Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
Gomez got her acting break on Disney series Raven's Home and Netflix show The Baby-Sitters Club, before being cast in 2022's Doctor Strange sequel as America Chavez. Since then, however, her acting output has been limited, though she did take part (and win) the 2023 season of Dancing with the Stars.
Speaking to Bustle, Gomez said her MCU role as the multiverse-punching teenager had dissuaded filmmakers from casting her in other projects — and that despite seeking other work, she had suffered from the assumption that she'd now become too expensive to hire or, alternatively, that she would be unavailable due to her potentially being busy filming further Marvel appearances.
The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday
"After [Doctor Strange], I had a hard time getting roles," Gomez told . "They were like, 'She's too expensive. What if she's in this and that, her schedule?' And I'm like, 'Guys...'
"It was a gift and a curse," she continued, "because I was like, 'Wait, I want to do the cool indie movies. Give me a chance, guys.'"
It's something of an odd situation as, in reality, Gomez has not returned as America Chavez in any subsequent Marvel project, despite her portrayal of the character being generally well received.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness ends with Chavez heading off to train alongside other sorcerers at Kamar-Taj, seemingly setting up her up as an even more powerful superhero when she next pops up. Four years later, however, and there's been no mention of her ever turning up again. For a while, rumors persisted that Marvel was considering a magical school series entitled Strange Academy that may have continued the Kamar-Taj storyline, but nothing is yet to materialize.
There's been no confirmation of Chavez turning up in Avengers: Doomsday or the subesequent Avengers: Secret Wars, either, despite her multiversal powers seemingly being a good fit for a pair of movies that are set to wrap up the MCU's Multiverse Saga. But perhaps her return is being kept as a surprise?
"Well, they own the rights to my image, so it's possible," Gomez concluded, when asked if she would appear in Doomsday next month.
Image credit: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images

item.title: Elon Musk has extended production of Cybertruck to work through an order backlog, the Tesla owner has said.
item.description:
Elon Musk has extended production of Cybertruck to work through an order backlog, the Tesla owner has said.
Last week, the tech billionaire confirmed plans to wind down production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory in Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production. Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill then suggested that Cybertruck was being discontinued.
But Musk said today that production will now be extended through the end of summer 2027. He did not put a firm date on the end of production, but did provide some commentary around the decision, saying: “This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what’s the point?”
Tesla Cybertruck Official Release - Slideshow
The angular Cybertruck launched in 2023 to much fanfare, but sales have been poor. Indeed, the truck has suffered online ridicule ever since it was introduced in 2019, when Musk himself shattered its supposed unbreakable glass during a live demo.
While fans of both Musk and Cybertruck have welcomed the news, there is no suggestion here that Tesla is making a long-term commitment to production of the vehicle. The focus, now, is on Cybercab, which Musk has said will play a crucial role in Tesla’s robotaxi plans. According to Reuters, the two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.
Photo by FREDERIC J. BROWN/AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
item.description:
The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios in a sudden and unexpected move that has sparked no end of worry and speculation among fans. Gunn, for his part, cited a distaste for the “corporate” side of the job, but confirmed that projects already in motion, like Man of Tomorrow, are still a-go.
Fans aren’t the only ones scratching their heads about what might happen next. Francis Lawrence, the director of oodles of Hollywood blockbusters, is also in this boat — though he’s rather optimistic about the situation, as it means he might finally get the chance to make another Constantine film.
Constantine: City of Demons Images
Speaking with Collider ahead of his next movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Lawrence clarified that he isn’t happy for anyone to lose their jobs, but admitted that he’s keen on the possibility of getting Constantine 2 off the ground now that things are changing at DC.
"Well, I’ll tell you this,” he began. “Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs, so this is not like a schadenfreude kind of thing, but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for twenty-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it, and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it.
“So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity. But again, we’ve been trying to make this for twenty-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine?'"
Lawrence said, without a doubt, that this version of Constantine will be another R-Rated film, no matter what. He explained that the first movie had been made with a PG-13 rating in mind, but despite their best efforts, it was hit with an R label. If given the chance to make a sequel, Lawrence wants to lean all-in and make it a true R-rated experience.
“So, part of the idea from the very beginning was, because we followed all the rules to make a PG-13 movie and we got hit with an R, they told us, 'You can’t do anything about it. It’s going to be an R no matter what.' We tried to fight them on it, and they said, 'Nope. It’s an R,' but really, it’s an R-rated PG-13 movie, which pisses me off,” he explained.
"And so we all kind of came back and said, 'Okay, when we do this next time, we’re making the hard-R version of Constantine.' So when we do it, it’s going to be the hard-R version of Constantine."
Lawrence doubled down on his desire to make another Constantine at all costs, even saying that he doesn’t mind if it gets put into a shared universe or remade to fit DC’s ever-evolving plans at some point. He claimed that he and Keanu would even compromise on their financial compensation to get the film made, if that's what it takes.
"Personally, I don’t even care if somebody has a plan for some sort of shared universe, and they want to do another version of Constantine. If they just let us do the sequel to our version, they can coexist. So, I have renewed hope as of yesterday that there might be some possibility for forward movement there,” he said.
"We have to be responsible,” he continued, speaking about the financial side of the equation. “We want to make it. This is not the kind of movie that I would charge full freight and Keanu could charge full freight. It’s something we have to do, because we love and want to take a gamble on it, and do it responsibly. And so, we’ve been thinking about that same idea for 20 years, that we’re not going to do it for $100 million. We have to be scrappy about it."
Constantine was released in 2005. Starring Keanu Reeves, the movie is based on the DC/Vertigo comic book Hellblazer and follows supernatural detective John Constantine in his mission to purge the world of nefarious evil entities.
This is the latest news about Constantine after Reeves reportedly pitched a sequel to DC Studios in 2025. And just earlier this month, it was revealed that Evil Dead Wrath writer-director Francis Galluppi was hired by DC Studios to write a John Constantine movie for them, though it’s unclear if he’ll also be directing.

item.title: Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, Amy Hennig's Captain America/Black Panther game, is reportedly close to being finished, but it sounds like it may be extremely compromised.
item.description:
Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, Amy Hennig's Captain America/Black Panther game, is reportedly close to being finished, but it could be extremely compromised.
According to a new report from Kotaku, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra is "close to done." The news comes hours after rumors began spread online that the game was canceled, with an official announcement coming soon. According to Kotaku and Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, Skydancer leadership told staff via Slack that this is not the case and that they should continue business as usual.
Kotaku's report went on to describe the game's development as difficult, which should come as no surprise to anyone who's been following its journey. The title was announced in 2024 and has been delayed several times, with little to no news or footage beyond that.
Marvel 1943 Unreal 5.4 Demo Screenshots
Kotaku claims that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra initially began as a Netflix game, but was later expanded for consoles and PC. Unfortunately, the title is reportedly "light on gameplay," with most of the action mapped to one button and the experience lacking "significant interactivity."
The project has also allegedly gone well over budget, and as a result, has had to "significantly" scale back from its original vision in terms of content and length. As of right now, we have no idea when Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra will release, but if it really is nearing the finish line, we could see something next year. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like the game will be a hyper-engaging action/adventure title with riveting action, from the sound of it.
This is purely speculative, but based on the details from Kotaku's report, it wouldn't be surprising if this is more along the lines of a Quantic Dream experience like Heavy Rain or Detroit: Become Human, with some combat sprinkled in. Either way, if fans were hoping for something like Marvel's Spider-Man, but with Captain America and Black Panther, they may end up pretty disappointed.
Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra is meant to be director Amy Hennig's first proper game since Uncharted 3 in 2011. Although she has consulted and helped out on some other games like Forspoken over the years, Hennig hasn't led a new game since Uncharted 3. She was reportedly ousted from Naughty Dog in the early 2010s after Uncharted 4 was struggling to meet internal expectations. She then went to EA, where she was meant to lead a new Star Wars game with Visceral Games, but the studio was shut down and the project was scrapped. Now, she's heading up this Marvel game... and we'll just have to wait and see how it turns out.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: So many Marvel fans tried to snag their tickets for Avengers: Doomsday after watching the VisionQuest season finale that they literally crashed the AMC Theaters app.
item.description:
So many Marvel fans tried to snag their tickets for Avengers: Doomsday after watching the VisionQuest season finale that they literally crashed the AMC Theatres app. At least, that's what users are saying.
The crash reportedly occurred on the night of November 10 — the same night that the VisionQuest finale aired, which included a post-credits scene that all but confirmed a particular character will show up in Avengers: Doomsday.
Shortly after the episode aired on Disney+, fans and Marvel fanpages shared that the AMC app was showing an error message when they tried to use it, which asked them to “please try again.” They were unable to navigate to other pages within the app; it seems that it was totally unusable during this time.
VisionQuest Images
Of course, viewers instantly pointed to the VisionQuest season finale as the reason for this, indicating that the hype levels were high enough to warrant a mass of fan interest in seeing Doomsday in theaters.
In a statement to IGN, an AMC Theatres spokesperson revealed that there was a 30-minute period where "some transactions were taking longer than normal." The spokesperson said that the AMC app didn't outright crash, as data showed that tickets continued to get sold throughout this period, but indicated that some users may have run into that error message during that time.
Warning: Major spoilers for VisionQuest below!
It’s no surprise that Marvel fans got so excited about Doomsday after this. The finale’s post-credits scene, which was also kept a secret from the media, showed Wanda Maximoff, aka the Scarlet Witch, having an interaction with Doctor Doom.
The specific scene returns to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, in which the Scarlet Witch sacrifices herself by destroying the Darkhold. While viewers were under the impression that her heroic decision ultimately lead to her death, this isn’t the case. Doctor Doom appears and frees her from the rubble that had collapsed on top of her, saying, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." She comes to with a shocked expression before the scene ends.
Given that the Scarlet Witch has been officially confirmed to be alive after four years of ambiguity, fans are understandably beside themselves with excitement. On social media, viewers wasted no time sharing their hype for the scene in response to AMC’s app crash, with one writing, “That’s the Scarlet Witch effect!”
“Wanda impact,” another wrote, while another said the crash happened “all because of Wanda Maximoff!”
“Mother is that powerful,” another superfan said. “We’re ready to support anything she does because she can do no wrong.”
How are you feeling about the future of Marvel post Avengers: Doomsday?

item.title: Three days after launching an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, the Nvidia board is reportedly preparing to oust the executive.
item.description:
Three days after launching an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, the Nvidia board is reportedly preparing to oust the executive.
Nvidia's board will be meeting as soon as today to discuss Huang's future after an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy, according to The Wall Street Journal. That affair was first reported by The New York Times and was followed up by a statement issued by Nvidia on Sunday, saying it'd be investigating its CEO. According to a new report from The New York Times, he'd also engaged in a second affair with an executive who reported to him.
This meeting follows an investigation that was announced on Sunday. In that announcement, Nvidia said, "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it."
Huang then issued a letter to employees, obtained by the BBC, where he admitted that he was unfaithful and apologized for hurting his wife and children.
In many ways, Jensen Huang is the face of AI in the U.S., and so it makes sense that Nvidia's board would want to get this situation under control. The company's chips power nearly every AI model that's currently running, and so a security breach of this scale is a massive liability. Huang is a co-founder of Nvidia and has been running the company since 1993, so his ousting could have huge ramifications.
IGN has reached out to Nvidia for comment and will update this story as soon as communications have been received.
Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: Henry Cavill has stated that he's still open to the idea of playing Superman following all the shake-ups at DC Studios.
item.description:
Henry Cavill has stated that he's still open to the idea of playing Superman following all the shake-ups at DC Studios.
In an interview with Inverse, Cavill was asked if he'd ever be interested in playing Superman again, and the interviewer suggested the Kingdom Come storyline as a possibility. Cavill noted he would never say never to the idea, and that there are a lot of "fantastic storylines" to adapt for Superman.
"Look, there's lots of fantastic storylines. There's always a lot of opportunity. As the pigeon sang to Fievel in An American Tail, 'never say never.' And I buy into that. I’ve had such a wonderful time playing Superman in the past. I would never say never now."
Ranking the Superman Actors
Of course, the timing of these comments could not come at a more interesting moment. If this happened a week ago, no one would've thought much of it. However, earlier this week, DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were ousted from the company. They remain on board until December 1, when a new head, Jeremy Latcham, will take over. Latcham is expected to make changes to DC's direction, possibly resulting in a reboot, though that has yet to be firmly decided. His ultimate vision, however, is to focus on DC's mainstream characters in an effort to quickly assemble the Justice League on the big screen.
Presumably, they'll wait until James Gunn's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, hits theaters in July to make a decision on whether they'll reboot or recast this DC universe. Cavill has famously been through a lot as Superman. His debut film, Man of Steel, was controversial thanks to the absurd casualties in his fight with General Zod. Batman v Superman also caused some friction with fans for a variety of reasons, one of which was that Superman was extremely brooding and miserable.
After the catastrophic disaster that was Justice League, Cavill's role as Superman remained in question. There were rumors he would be replaced, while others indicated the powers that be simply weren't sure what to do with him. Eventually, Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson went above all of the WB execs and brought the actor back for a cameo in 2022's Black Adam, five years after Cavill's last appearance in the role. He was promised new Superman adventures... but then, James Gunn took over DC just weeks later, and Cavill was essentially let go from the role.
The fact that Cavill is open to taking another crack at things after all of that is certainly interesting. Whether that opportunity ever comes remains to be seen, but it seems hard to imagine the new leadership reviving the Snyderverse.
Do you want to see Skydance reboot the DCU?

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever is off to a monumental start, with more players wandering Azeroth than ever before. And at least one death metal guitarist can't put it down long enough to watch his opener play.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever is off to a monumental start, with more players wandering Azeroth than ever before. And at least one death metal guitarist can't put it down long enough to watch his opener play.
Death metal band Archspire posted a video to Instagram, overlaid with text that reads, "POV World of Warcraft Forever comes out the same day as the show," as the camera shows a Steam Deck with an undead Warlock running around with his voidwalker. The caption carries on the bit, saying, "When your set starts at 9:00 but you just zoned into Undercity to pick up your Voidwalker quest so you can pet-tank your way through Fenris Isle."
I get the appeal, some of the quests in Fenris Isle are absolutely brutal if you don't have anyone else in your party, so getting a purple blob that can tank it for you really is exciting. It doesn't hurt that WoW Forever runs incredibly on a handheld, either.
WoW Forever's newfound controller support and lightweight system requirements make it a natural match for handheld gaming PCs. I've tested the game on both the Xbox Ally X and the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, and both have been able to handle the game at pretty high settings without dipping below 60 fps. I haven't played the game on the Steam Deck quite yet, but at least from Archspire's Instagram post, it seems to be running just fine.
Archspire's guitarist is also not the only Death Metaller who loves WoW. IGN interviewed Cannibal Corpse way back in 2008, and when we asked George "Corpsegrinder" Fisher about his love for the game, he told us, "It is true, I am obsessed with WOW! I have 70 level 70 characters. I play HORDE side ONLY. I hate the Alliance with a passion!"
Corpsegrinder also told us a story about how he was inundated with messages from fans, saying, "I did another interview where I said my Rogue's name and the server I played on, and then I started getting tells in game. A LOT OF TELLS. I was getting bombarded even when I was raiding, so I transferred him off the server and changed his name. I loved talking to people who were into Cannibal Corpse, but it was getting so I logged in and couldn't play, because all I did was exchange tells with people."
A lot has changed since 2008, but WoW Forever is looking to recapture some of that old-school WoW magic. And just based on how many people are playing the game, Blizzard seems to have pulled it off, even though they've run into some hurdles with gold rewards and dungeon experience.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?
